draft.overall: MI leads this range, up 213 percent from the prior close, with fresh news found in our sources: a disclosed agreement to sell Class A shares in a private placement. The next covered gainers by move are SAIQ, up 286 percent from the prior close, with only older or secondary news in our sources, and APUS, up 64 percent from the prior close, with fresh news found in our sources: an agreement with BlockAssure to build and operate an insurance network. 3 of the 12 names the desk covers had fresh news in our sources.

lines.text: Up 221.3% since the previous checkpoint and printed a new high of day. The catalyst in our sources is a 6-K filed at 16:20 ET on September 30, 2026, in which NFT Ltd disclosed an agreement to sell 80,000,000 Class A ordinary shares to non-U.S. purchasers at $0.45 per share for approximately $36 million in a private placement subject to closing conditions, not reported as a completed issuance; the desk reads the proposed placement as large next to the last reported outstanding count, which is stale and cannot set a dilution percentage, with the purchase price below the market price in hand, and our sources do not report whether the placement closed, whether shares were issued, or when any issued shares could be resold.

The catalyst in our sources is an 8-K at 07:00 ET on October 5, 2026 disclosing a September 30, 2026 license agreement with Genentech covering certain GCase candidates, under which Genentech leads development, regulatory, manufacturing and commercialization while Alector retains its Alector Brain Carrier platform and rights to its wholly owned pipeline, and Alector said the deal extends its cash runway into 2029. The desk reads it as a company-specific validation and funding-runway event for a development-stage neurodegeneration name, with the upfront payment, milestones, royalties and total transaction value not stated in our sources.

Printed a new high of day. This is not a fresh catalyst: the latest commercial news in our sources is the July 9, 2026 Fosun Diagnostics commercial supply agreement and a July 16 shareholder update, both stale against the market date, while the September filings cover an effective warrant-resale registration and ATM capacity rather than new business; the desk reads the Fosun agreement as a legitimate commercial-expansion story that is not timely enough to explain the present move, and our sources do not say whether it has produced material revenue.

This is not a fresh catalyst: QTREX reported in a 6-K at 13:20 ET on October 1, 2026 that a leading quantum computing company independently tested its cryogenic interconnect at 20 mK and measured over 100 dB of channel isolation across the 4 to 8 GHz qubit band, and said it was finalizing a binding definitive agreement with that unnamed company, with the name and full agreement to be disclosed within weeks. The desk reads the isolation result as the material metric behind a concrete quantum-infrastructure story, while the counterparty identity, contract value and any commercial economics are not disclosed, and the agreement was not reported as executed.

This is not a fresh catalyst: Reliance reported on October 1, 2026 that it completed the sale of Altruis Benefit Consulting for $8 million in cash plus a potential earnout of up to $1 million, and a secondary report at 08:23 ET on October 5, 2026 said the company repaid its approximately $4.4 million Oak Street term loan in full with no term debt outstanding. The desk reads the sale as material cash proceeds and the repayment as deleveraging, noting the repayment rests only on secondary coverage and that our sources do not show how much of the proceeds remains after debt, costs and holdbacks.

Down 37.5% since the previous checkpoint. This is not a fresh catalyst: WISeSat.Space completed its business combination with Columbus Acquisition Corp. on October 1, 2026 and its ordinary shares began Nasdaq trading as SAIQ on October 2, per 6-K filings, with no transaction value or operating result stated in the primary excerpts; the desk reads the listing as a corporate transition that can concentrate attention and trading in the first sessions, with no primary-source valuation, redemption outcome, post-closing cash or capitalization detail in our sources.

The catalyst in our sources is MindWave's announced agreement with BlockAssure to build and operate AssureChain, an insurance and reinsurance network, which secondary coverage at 08:03 ET on October 5, 2026 describes as a two-year contract with MindWave to receive 20% of the planned token supply and fees not disclosed. The desk reads it as a new customer agreement for MindWave's technology-services business with a token component, leaving the direct financial impact unquantified since cash fees, token valuation and sale restrictions are not stated, and our sources do not show whether the move began before or after the announcement.
ICU is not researched yet; there is no dossier at this checkpoint.

Printed a new high of day. This is not a fresh catalyst: ReTo announced at 11:03 ET on September 29, 2026 a 1-for-20 reverse split effective October 2, following a September 18 announcement of a $15 million registered direct offering of 10,000,000 Class A shares and 10,000,000 warrants whose closing is not reported in our sources, and a halt at 19:50 ET on October 1, 2026 was labeled news pending with no underlying news in the bundle; the desk reads the split as arriving alongside recently announced potential share and warrant issuance, with the offering close, any issued-share total and any warrant exercises unreported.

Printed a new high of day. This is not a fresh catalyst: on October 1, 2026 Veea announced an agreement with TROLLEE Holdings for phased deployment of VeeaONE across 1,000 unattended stores, with secondary coverage that day pairing the announcement with an approximately 48% stock move; the desk reads the planned deployment as a potentially material commercial use of VeeaONE, while contract value, schedule, purchase commitments, exclusivity and expected revenue are not disclosed in our sources.

Down 18.0% since the previous checkpoint and lost $1.17 support. This is not a fresh catalyst: a 6-K at 10:32 ET on September 30, 2026 disclosed a September 23 equity purchase agreement giving VCIG the right, subject to conditions, to direct Hudson Global Ventures to buy up to $125 million of ordinary shares, along with Dune and FirstFire convertible-note deals, and a September 29 F-1 seeks registration of up to 100,000,000 ELOC purchase shares plus warrant and conversion shares; the desk reads it as financing with large dollar capacity and substantial potential issuance if conditions, registration, conversion or exercise requirements are met, with no put notice, no ELOC purchase and no F-1 effectiveness shown in our sources.

Printed a new high of day. The research could not tell whether a catalyst is at work: SEC filings, including an 8-K at 16:30 ET on September 23, 2026, document completion of the business combination, the renaming of HVII as ONE Nuclear Energy Inc., the Nasdaq listing of ONEN and approximately $146.5 million of redemption payments, but coverage is SEC-only with no newsroom or newswire sources, so the desk reads it as a completed de-SPAC that followed heavy redemptions and may shape post-combination trading, without being able to tie the timing of the current move to that closing.
